acid-base-titration.name: Acid–Base Titration Calculator
acid-base-titration.intro: Compute titration volume and equivalence-point pH from the mole balance of H⁺ and OH⁻: V_eq = C_base·V_base / C_acid.

arrhenius.name: Arrhenius Equation Calculator
arrhenius.intro: Estimate a reaction rate constant at any temperature from k = A·exp(−Ea / (R·T)).

boiling-point-elevation.name: Boiling Point Elevation Calculator
boiling-point-elevation.intro: Compute the boiling point elevation of a solution from ΔTb = Kb·m·i (molality × ebullioscopic constant × van ’t Hoff factor).

buffer-ph.name: Buffer pH Calculator (Henderson–Hasselbalch)
buffer-ph.intro: Estimate buffer pH from pH = pKa + log([A⁻] / [HA]) using conjugate base and acid concentrations.

dilution-c1v1.name: Solution Dilution Calculator (C₁V₁ = C₂V₂)
dilution-c1v1.intro: Solve for any one of concentration or volume before/after dilution using C₁V₁ = C₂V₂.

empirical-formula.name: Empirical Formula Calculator
empirical-formula.intro: Derive the simplest whole-number atom ratio (empirical formula) from a percent composition or mass data.

gas-density.name: Gas Density Calculator
gas-density.intro: Compute gas density from ρ = (P·M) / (R·T) using pressure, molar mass and temperature.

gibbs-free-energy.name: Gibbs Free Energy Calculator
gibbs-free-energy.intro: Predict reaction spontaneity from ΔG = ΔH − T·ΔS; ΔG < 0 means spontaneous at the given temperature.

ideal-gas-volume.name: Ideal Gas Volume Calculator
ideal-gas-volume.intro: Find gas volume from the ideal gas law V = n·R·T / P.

kp-kc.name: Kp–Kc Converter
kp-kc.intro: Convert between equilibrium constants using Kp = Kc·(R·T)^Δn, where Δn is the change in moles of gas.

limiting-reagent.name: Limiting Reagent Calculator
limiting-reagent.intro: Identify the limiting reactant and theoretical yield from stoichiometric amounts of each reagent.

mass-fraction.name: Mass Fraction Calculator
mass-fraction.intro: Compute mass fraction w = m_component / m_total of a substance in a mixture.

mass-to-moles.name: Mass to Moles Converter
mass-to-moles.intro: Convert mass to amount of substance using n = m / M (molar mass).

molality.name: Molality Calculator
molality.intro: Compute molality b = n_solute / m_solvent (moles of solute per kilogram of solvent).

molarity.name: Molarity Calculator
molarity.intro: Compute molarity c = n / V (moles of solute per litre of solution), or convert mass to molarity.

mole-fraction.name: Mole Fraction Calculator
mole-fraction.intro: Compute mole fraction x_i = n_i / Σn for each component in a mixture.

nernst-equation.name: Nernst Equation Calculator
nernst-equation.intro: Compute electrode potential E = E° − (R·T / n·F)·lnQ under non-standard conditions.

normality.name: Normality Calculator
normality.intro: Compute normality N = z·M (equivalents of solute per litre), where z is the equivalence factor.

partial-pressure.name: Partial Pressure Calculator (Dalton’s Law)
partial-pressure.intro: Compute a gas component’s partial pressure from p_i = x_i·P_total using mole (or volume) fraction.

ph-from-ka.name: pH from Ka Calculator
ph-from-ka.intro: Estimate the pH of a weak acid solution from [H⁺] = √(Ka·C) (valid for small dissociation).

ph-to-h.name: pH to [H⁺] Converter
ph-to-h.intro: Convert pH to hydrogen ion concentration: [H⁺] = 10^(−pH).

poh-to-ph.name: pOH to pH Converter
poh-to-ph.intro: Convert pOH to pH using pH + pOH = 14.00 at 25 °C (and pOH = −log[OH⁻]).

reaction-quotient.name: Reaction Quotient (Q) Calculator
reaction-quotient.intro: Compute the reaction quotient Q from species concentrations or partial pressures to compare with K.

resistivity-from-r.name: Resistivity from Resistance Calculator
resistivity-from-r.intro: Compute resistivity ρ = R·A / L from measured resistance, cross-section area and length.

solubility-product.name: Solubility Product (Ksp) Calculator
solubility-product.intro: Compute Ksp or molar solubility from ion concentrations: Ksp = [A]^m·[B]^n.

solution-dilution.name: Solution Dilution Calculator
solution-dilution.intro: Dilute a stock solution to a target concentration using C₁V₁ = C₂V₂, solving for any unknown.
